title: Each `Core\Task` child is charged its whole 1 MiB stack reservation, so a memory cap counts stack pages the task never touches.
text: `Child::new` charges `STACK_CHARGE`, which is `TASK_STACK_SIZE` (`1 << 20`, `crates/nvs-host/src/stack.rs:88`), with `nvs_runtime::budget::carry` (`crates/nvs-host/src/group.rs:399`), and `Drop for Child` credits it back (`crates/nvs-host/src/group.rs:499`). `Core\Task::map` holds a `Child` for every element at once, so N children are charged N MiB together even when each finishes at once. The charge is the same with or without `--config`: what differs is the cap. The shipped defaults set no `[limits] memory` (`crates/nvs-config/src/default.toml:68`), so `nvs run` with no config file counts the charge and enforces nothing, and 4096 children use 26 MB of real memory. The repository's `nvs.toml` sets 256M, which every ladder runs under, so `scheduler/waiters.nvs` and `scheduler/parked.nvs` stop at 128 parked tasks. Smaller stacks that grow, or charging touched pages, are the two answers. The first changes how deep a task may recurse, which is observable behaviour and goes under *Decisions for you*. Ladder: `scheduler/tasks.nvs` with the bytes column read per task.
